done_state: Given warehouse rollup data and an injected ticket-rollup dict (the real live TESSERA read is out of scope here, per every other component's own established pattern), the snapshot publisher writes index.json and per-project shards matching ARCHITECTURE.md section 17's documented shape into a new generation directory and flips the current symlink to it last -- never mutating a prior generation, never publishing a torn or partial generation -- retains generations by the age-AND-count rule section 7 specifies, and refuses to publish (leaving current unchanged) when the warehouse is not genuinely clean or the snapshot_ticket_rollup_identity check fails against the supplied ticket rollup.

criteria.statement: publish() writes every file of a new generation into a freshly-created gen-<timestamp>/ directory and flips the current symlink to it only after every file in that directory is fully written -- never mutating an existing generation directory in place.
criteria.verification: atlas/snapshot/tests/test_publish_atomicity.py: calls publish() twice with different fixture data, asserts each call creates a NEW gen-*/ directory distinct from the last, asserts the first generation's files are byte-identical before and after the second publish (never mutated), and asserts current always points at the most recently completed generation, never a partially-written one (checked by asserting index.json is present and parses inside every generation current has ever pointed to during the test).

criteria.statement: A reader that resolves current once and then reads files under that resolved path is guaranteed a consistent generation even if publish() is called again afterward -- the old generation's files remain valid and unchanged at their resolved path (never deleted while it could still be the most recent generation kept by C3's retention rule).
criteria.verification: atlas/snapshot/tests/test_publish_atomicity.py: resolves current to a real path, publishes again, re-reads the ORIGINAL resolved path's index.json, asserts it is unchanged and still parses -- the old generation was not deleted or mutated out from under an in-progress reader.

criteria.statement: Retention keeps a generation only when it is younger than max_age_seconds OR is among the newest 3 generations -- ARCHITECTURE.md section 7's age-AND-count rule, tested with an injectable clock since real wall-clock time cannot be controlled in a fast unit test.
criteria.verification: atlas/snapshot/tests/test_retention.py: publishes 6 generations with a fake clock advancing past max_age_seconds between some of them, asserts the on-disk generation set after each publish matches exactly what the rule predicts -- old-and-not-in-newest-3 generations are removed, young or newest-3 generations survive.

criteria.statement: publish() refuses to write a new generation or move current when the warehouse's query-facade status() is not genuinely clean, or when snapshot_ticket_rollup_identity fails against the supplied ticket rollup -- both refusals leave the filesystem exactly as it was before the call, not a partial write.
criteria.verification: atlas/snapshot/tests/test_publish_refusal.py: two separate tests, one with a non-clean warehouse fixture and one with a ticket_rollup dict whose open_total deliberately does not equal open_null_severity + sum(open_by_severity), both asserting publish() raises and current/generation-directory-list are byte-for-byte unchanged from before the call.

criteria.statement: index.json's shape matches ARCHITECTURE.md section 17 exactly for a real fixture: schema_version, generated_at, refresh_cadence_seconds, max_age_seconds (derived as 3x refresh_cadence_seconds per section 5, not independently configurable), warehouse_run_id, cursors, verdict_window_days, rate_uninterpretable_handlers, severity_rubric, roots, unresolved_scopes, and a projects block with open_total/open_by_severity/open_null_severity/open_null_tier/root_state/root_is_shared/tickets per project, with the open_total identity holding for every project (guaranteed by C4's refusal on violation).
criteria.verification: atlas/snapshot/tests/test_index_shape.py: publishes against a multi-project fixture, parses the resulting index.json, asserts every documented top-level key is present with the correct type, and asserts max_age_seconds == 3 * refresh_cadence_seconds exactly.

criteria.statement: A project shard whose source_root is shared with another registered prefix (the real FORE/AREM shape) sets rollup_scope='<ambiguous>' and rollup_is_shared_with naming the other prefix(es) -- ARCHITECTURE.md section 6's 'no consumer can read FORE's rollup as FORE's alone.'
criteria.verification: atlas/snapshot/tests/test_shard_sharing.py: fixture with two projects sharing one source_root, publishes, asserts both shards' rollup_scope='<ambiguous>' and rollup_is_shared_with correctly names the other; a third, non-shared project's shard has rollup_scope equal to its own prefix and rollup_is_shared_with empty.

failure_criteria.statement: A publish that fails partway (a write error on one shard file) leaves current pointing at a generation directory with some files missing or half-written.
failure_criteria.detection: publish() writes all files for a generation BEFORE flipping current -- a failure before the flip leaves current at the prior (complete) generation, never the new (incomplete) one; a test simulating a mid-write failure asserts current is unchanged.

failure_criteria.statement: A generation count, retention window, or file-size number in this component's code comments or commit messages has no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the component's source and commit messages for numeric claims; each must name the command or test that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: The publisher assumes the snapshot root directory exists, rather than creating it or reporting a named failure.
failure_criteria.detection: publish() creates the snapshot root and its generation subdirectory if absent, with a real filesystem test asserting this against a root that does not yet exist.

failure_criteria.statement: A publish refusal (C4) is logged to a channel nobody reads instead of being raised to the caller.
failure_criteria.detection: Every refusal is a raised, named exception the caller/test directly asserts on.

out_of_scope: The real live TESSERA read (tessera_to_snapshot interface) -- this component consumes an injected ticket_rollup dict of the same shape a real TESSERA read would produce, matching resolve's own established pattern of consuming injected registry data. Real end-to-end wiring against the live TESSERA store is foreman:integration-test's job.
hookclient, the reference reader of this artifact -- a separate component with its own GOALS.json, consuming exactly the format this component's tests already pin down in C5/C6.
The severity rubric content itself (still blocked) -- section 17's severity_rubric.status='absent' path is the only one this component builds, matching the architecture document's own stated blocker.

Concurrent-writer SQLite lock behavior (section 5's measured 59.9ms busy-timeout failure) -- that is about the warehouse read path under a concurrent writer, not this component's own publish mechanism.
constraints: Zero third-party dependencies -- Python 3 stdlib only (json, pathlib, os for the atomic symlink flip), matching this environment's established convention.

The symlink flip uses os.symlink to a temp name plus os.replace (or an equivalent atomic rename), never a two-step unlink-then-symlink, matching ARCHITECTURE.md section 7's own recorded gap about needing this specified.

Tests use Python's stdlib unittest and an injectable clock (never real datetime.now() for retention timing), matching every other component's own convention plus this component's specific need for deterministic time-based tests.
